decision: Should ADRs ship with a Status field?
reason:
Use a required Status field with a small vocabulary: Proposed, Accepted, Superseded, and Rejected. This lets templates, reviewers, and future indexers share one explicit contract instead of reconstructing state from prose.

The field belongs in every ADR header because downstream tools need a stable location. Existing ADRs can be migrated together so mixed formats do not persist.
tradeoff: A required field makes hand-written ADRs slightly more formal and requires coordinated migration of existing documents.

facets.label: Contract
facets.text: Generators and consumers depend on the same field and vocabulary.

facets.label: Coordination
facets.text: Templates, existing ADRs, and review guidance must change together.
